title: Roaring Silence: Can We Break the Chains of Illegal Wildlife Trade?

tasks: Task 1: Design 5-year STSEA project via RBM+LFA
Task 2: Select client via EWM 3-level indicators (WWF=78.70)
Task 3: Model WWF-Interpol cooperation via expected utility
Task 4: Evaluate impact via ridge regression (R2=0.991)
Task 5: Communicate via one-page memorandum to WWF

section_map.summary: Comprehensive strategy for combating IWT targeting tigers in SEA
764 projects trend analysis, STSEA design with RBM+LFA
EWM 3-level indicators, WWF selected (78.70), GRA for tiger justification
WWF-Interpol cooperation via optimal expected utility

contributions.summary: Trend analysis of 764 former IWT projects to identify SEA as priority area.
Three-level EWM indicator system for IO client assessment across 7 organizations.
GRA ranking of species: Tigers (0.83) > Live reptiles (0.80) > European eels (0.76).
Optimal expected utility proof that cooperation raises detection rate and reduces ITT.
Ridge regression (lambda=0.022, R2=0.991) for project impact prediction.

dependency_graph.handoff: Client selection (WWF) feeds into GRA justification for tiger focus
Cooperation benefit (detection rate) feeds into regression as explanatory variable

assumptions.summary: Future Counter-IWT projects will be consistent with current total trend.
An effective Counter-IWT project should be specific and trans-regional.
Individuals make decisions by logically pursuing self-interest to maximize utility.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Data from IWT Database (764 projects), UN Comtrade, UNODC Statistics.
Missing data handled via regression, averaging methods.

models.summary: EWM: Three-level indicator system with TOPSIS for client scoring.
GRA: Grey Relational Analysis for species ranking in SEA.
OEUM: Optimal Expected Utility Model for cooperation benefit.
RR: Ridge Regression for impact evaluation with 4 OVIs.

verification.summary: Initial MLR VIF check reveals multicollinearity; ridge regression resolves.
Testing set prediction matches historical data (Figure 12).

results_trace.summary: SEA identified as trending area from 764 projects funding analysis.
WWF selected with highest score 78.70/100 among 7 IOs.
Tigers rank highest (0.83) in GRA correlation with total SEA trafficking.
Detection rate increase proven to reduce ITT investment (dy*/d(alpha)<0).
Terrestrial protected area size is most sensitive variable for tiger trade reduction.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: 764 projects data-driven area selection demonstrates thorough background research.
Expected utility model provides rigorous economic proof for cooperation benefit.
Multicollinearity detection and ridge regression show statistical sophistication.

weaknesses.summary: Natural shortcomings of mathematical models affect practical application.
Insufficient environmental knowledge limits variable completeness.
Only 7 annual data points for regression with 4 variables.

independent_extensions.summary: Extend utility model to multi-party coalition with varying detection rates.
Replace ridge with elastic net or LASSO for variable selection.

Grey Relational Analysis for species prioritization under data uncertainty.

unresolved_questions.question: How is TOPSIS applied to normalize the EWM-weighted scores to 0-100?
What specific functional forms are used for utility and penalty cost functions?
